ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Set I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}, and let R := Q[x_s : s in I] be the polynomial ring graded by deg(x_s) = s for each s in I. For each positive integer d define M_d(u,v) := |{m in Z : u < m <= v and d divides m}|. Assume M_d(r+a, r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for every positive integer d. Then there exists a family (f_s)_{s in I} of homogeneous polynomials in R such that deg(f_s) = r+s for every s in I, and the ordered list of these polynomials in increasing order of s is a regular sequence in R. If I is empty, this means the empty family.

ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let a, b, r, j be integers with 0 <= a <= b, r >= 0, and 0 <= j <= floor(r (b - a) / 2). Put I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}. For each positive integer d, define M_d(u,v) := |{m in Z : u < m <= v and d divides m}|, and assume M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for every positive integer d. Let X_j be the set of pairs (S, lambda) such that S is a subset of I, lambda is a finite multiset of elements of I, |lambda| denotes the sum of the elements of lambda, and |lambda| + sum_{s in S} (r + s) = j. Then there exists an involution iota_j : X_j -> X_j such that: (1) if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S',lambda') != (S,lambda), then |S'| is congruent to |S| + 1 modulo 2; and (2) if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S,lambda), then |S| is even.

payload.proof_nl:
Let I = (u_1,...,u_m) and B = A/I, and for each j let w_j be the image of v_j in B. For each integer t with 0 <= t <= n, set J_t = (u_1,...,u_m,v_1,...,v_t) in A, with J_0 = I. Because the concatenated sequence u_1,...,u_m,v_1,...,v_n is regular in A, two facts hold: each J_t is a proper ideal of A, and for each j with 1 <= j <= n, the element v_j is a nonzerodivisor on A/J_{j-1}.

First we prove the proper-ideal condition in B. Fix t with 0 <= t <= n. Suppose that the ideal (w_1,...,w_t) is all of B. Then there are elements b_1,...,b_t in B such that 1 = sum b_i w_i in B; when t = 0 this just means 1 = 0 in B. Choose lifts a_i in A of the elements b_i. Then 1 - sum a_i v_i lies in I, so 1 lies in I + (v_1,...,v_t) = J_t. This contradicts the fact that J_t is proper. Hence (w_1,...,w_t) is a proper ideal of B for every t. In particular, taking t = 0 shows that B is not the zero ring.

Next we prove the nonzerodivisor condition. Fix j with 1 <= j <= n. Let x be an element of A whose class in B/(w_1,...,w_{j-1}) is annihilated by w_j. By definition of the quotient, this means that v_j x lies in I + (v_1,...,v_{j-1}) = J_{j-1}. Since v_j is a nonzerodivisor on A/J_{j-1}, it follows that x lies in J_{j-1}. But then the class of x in B/(w_1,...,w_{j-1}) is zero. Therefore multiplication by w_j on B/(w_1,...,w_{j-1}) is injective, so w_j is a nonzerodivisor there.

Thus every initial ideal (w_1,...,w_t) is proper in B, and each w_j is a nonzerodivisor modulo the preceding ones. Hence w_1,...,w_n is a regular sequence in B = A/(u_1,...,u_m).

Now assume A is graded and all u_i and v_j are homogeneous. Then I = (u_1,...,u_m) is a homogeneous ideal, so B = A/I inherits the quotient grading, and the quotient map A -> B preserves degrees. Therefore the image w_j of a homogeneous element v_j of degree d lies in the degree-d part of B. Since w_j is nonzero by the regularity already proved, this means that w_j is homogeneous of degree d, so it has the same degree as v_j. This proves the graded statement as well.

m and n are finite lengths of the sequence; the statement does not specify whether they may be zero, but the standard reading allows empty sequences.

The phrase regular sequence carries the usual commutative algebra meaning: each element is a nonzerodivisor modulo the ideal generated by the earlier ones, and the generated ideal is proper at each stage.
The quotient is by the ideal generated by u_1 through u_m.

Homogeneous means each u_i and v_j lies entirely in one graded piece.
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: A regular sequence in a commutative ring remains regular after passing to the quotient by the ideal generated by an initial block of the sequence. If the ring is graded and the elements are homogeneous, then their images in the quotient stay homogeneous with the same degrees.

Then in the quotient ring B equal to A modulo the ideal generated by u_1 through u_m, the images bar_v_1 through bar_v_n form a regular sequence.
If A is graded and every u_i and v_j is homogeneous, then each bar_v_j is homogeneous and has the same degree as v_j.

payload.statement_nl: Let A be a commutative ring, and let u_1,...,u_m,v_1,...,v_n be a regular sequence in A. Then the images of v_1,...,v_n in the quotient ring A/(u_1,...,u_m) form a regular sequence. If A is graded and all u_i and v_j are homogeneous, then the quotient images are homogeneous and keep the same degrees.

detailed_findings.finding: The proof correctly verifies the proper-ideal condition for all initial segments in the quotient, including the t = 0 case.
The nonzerodivisor argument is complete and uses exactly the needed regularity property of the concatenated sequence modulo J_{j-1}.
The graded conclusion is properly reduced to the fact that quotient by a homogeneous ideal preserves homogeneity and degree of nonzero homogeneous images.

result_payload.reason: The proof is the standard and correct descent argument for regular sequences under quotient by an initial block. It proves that each initial ideal generated by the images of v_1,...,v_t is proper in B by lifting a hypothetical relation 1 = sum b_i w_i back to A and contradicting properness of J_t. It then proves that each w_j is a nonzerodivisor on B/(w_1,...,w_{j-1}) by lifting an annihilated class to x in A, observing v_j x \in J_{j-1}, and using that v_j is a nonzerodivisor on A/J_{j-1}. This matches the semantic sketch exactly. The graded addendum is also correctly justified since I is homogeneous, the quotient inherits the grading, and the image of a homogeneous v_j remains homogeneous of the same degree; nonzeroness from regularity avoids ambiguity about degree.
